idiom_name: std::views::iota/transform as the unfold + std::ranges::fold_left (C++23) or std::accumulate over the view as the fold
implementation_notes: C++20 ranges turn the unfold into a view: std::views::iota (or a custom view / views::transform / views::take_while chain) is the coalgebra, and the fold half is std::ranges::fold_left (C++23) or std::accumulate over the view's iterators (C++20). Views are lazy and their adaptors compose without materializing anything, so the pipeline evaluates element by element - precisely the deforestation a hylomorphism describes - and the result is produced without an intermediate container. Prefer this when the generation can be expressed as views; reach for std::generator (C++23) when the unfold needs irregular control flow, and for the hand-written driver when the abstraction's compile time or a std::function in the hot path would cost more than it saves.
pitfalls: Views are lazy but not owner-safe: a view over a temporary container dangles - the classic ranges lifetime trap - so keep the owning sequence alive for the whole pipeline.
std::ranges::fold_left is C++23; under C++20 the same pipeline must end in std::accumulate(begin, end, init, op), which needs the view's iterators.
A fold cannot short-circuit: needing the first match or an early failure means leaving the fold_left shape for ranges::find/any_of, or the code degenerates into an accumulate plus a flag.

variants.name: Hand-written fused driver over callables (C++11)
variants.idiom_name: hylo template / loop that applies the coalgebra and the algebra in one iteration
variants.implementation_notes: Where no lazy view vocabulary is available - or where the generator cannot be expressed as a view - the fusion is spelled out as a loop that calls the coalgebra for the next layer and applies the algebra to the accumulator in the same iteration, with both steps passed as callables (templates in the hot path, std::function when a stable interface is needed). The intermediate structure never exists, so the driver is the hylomorphism in its imperative form and the two halves stay independently testable. Choose it for pre-C++20 codebases, for irregular termination, and for hot paths where the ranges machinery would add type-erasure or compile-time overhead.
pitfalls: Type-erasing the two callables with std::function inside the loop costs an indirect call per element; keep them as template parameters or stateless lambdas.
Accumulator order must match the algebra's associativity: the loop folds left, so a right-associative combine needs an explicit stack or a reversed carrier.
The coalgebra returning std::optional makes the terminal case explicit, but a generator that never returns nullopt loops forever with nothing to inspect - test the descent, not just the aggregate.
